# Branch library opening hours — 2026-10-09

**Participants:** Moira Easterbrook (Branch Manager), Teo Lindahl (Librarian)

Moira: "We open at eight on Tuesdays and Thursdays so the commuter crowd can return books on the way in."

Teo: "And we close an hour earlier those days to keep the staffing flat."

evidence.quote: We open at eight on Tuesdays and Thursdays

observations.why: Flat, unhedged statement of an operational schedule with a stated reason; no ratification or settling is performed in the text, so the lower region applies.

evidence.quote: we close an hour earlier those days

observations.why: Plain assertive statement of a practice with a causal justification; it is firm but not framed as a ratified or recorded decision, so claim rather than decision.

Closing an hour earlier is framed as a cost-control trade-off against staffing, a proportionality move; torn with equality-matching (flat as even balance), but the cost-for-hours framing supports market-pricing most directly.

observations.why: States the closing schedule as fact with a staffing rationale; no request, threat, or argument is performed, so the read is informational only.

The map has no area or position on library hours, branch management, or staffing-flat scheduling. The People roster has neither Moira Easterbrook nor Teo Lindahl, so no person nodes bind. The one loose neighbour is the volunteer tool-library rota sample about weekday and Saturday staffing of returns, which I expanded to check for a shared frame. I did not expand the Documents entries for the bakery, bike stand, or greenhouse calls, or the cycling and pricing strata, because their spans do not touch opening hours or staffing schedules.

positions.name: BranchHoursAccessVersusStaffing
positions.frame: How are opening hours weighed when earlier access for one group of users is set against keeping staffing flat?
positions.why: Both statements set out one schedule change for the same two days: an 8am opening so commuters can return books, and an hour-earlier close to keep staffing flat. The frame reads both as one trade-off between access and staffing cost. Neither statement is a narrative's only support, and no existing stratum or narrative names opening hours, so no placement is proposed.

placements.why: The position holds one schedule change on the same two days: an 8am opening so commuters can return books, paired with an hour-earlier close to keep staffing flat. Both statements frame opening hours as a trade-off between access and staffing cost, a subject future envelopes about public service hours would keep feeding. No existing leaf holds opening hours. Narrative_BuyerReachablePricing shares a timing-for-access thread but concerns price changes, so it is recorded as a see-relation rather than a reuse. Narrative_InfrastructureWhereRidersNeedIt concerns where public infrastructure is placed, not when a service runs, so it does not hold this content. The leaf is standalone because nothing existing is close enough to be its parent.
